_meta.purpose: Maps historical claims already present in the Steinerne Brücke experience (fact cards, historical scroll, K-frame captions, 2.5D museum content) to source IDs registered in sources.json. NO_SOURCE -> claim stays explicitly unsupported; a claim is never marked SUPPORTED merely to fill this file in.

bridge_construction_period.claim: The Steinerne Brücke was built between 1135 and 1146.

bridge_15_piers.notes: Not an independently attested count in Q001 — follows directly from the validated 16-arch structure (16 arches between two abutments implies 15 intermediate piers). See SB_PIER_COUNT in the central SOURCE_REGISTRY for the identical reasoning.

bridge_length_300m.claim: The bridge is more than 300 metres long.

bridge_materials.claim: Materials used: limestone (Kalkstein), green sandstone (Grünsandstein), historic lime mortar, and a heterogeneous rubble fill core (Füllmauerwerk).
bridge_materials.notes: Q003 (OCR transcript) Aufnahme 041 / 087–088 / 108–109 per MUSEUM_CONTENT_MAP.json component sources.

pier_foundation_donaukies.claim: The medieval piers are founded directly on Danube gravel (Donaukies) — no forest of piles beneath the piers.
pier_foundation_donaukies.notes: Corrects a common misconception; must never be shown with piles under the main piers. Q003 Aufnahme 050–051.

beschlaechte_pier_protection.claim: A protective edge row (Beschlächte) of timber piles, wattle and stone protects the pier edges/riverbanks — distinct from the piers' own gravel foundation.

arch_construction_technique.claim: The arches were built over wooden centering frames (Lehrgerüst) and set with cranes; the 'Wolf' lifting clamp was used to move stone blocks.

bau_process_crane_technique.claim: 12th-century construction used simple wooden cranes, pulleys and winches; a wheel-crane is plausible but not certain.
bau_process_crane_technique.notes: MUSEUM_CONTENT_MAP.json marks this component's evidence_status as ESTIMATED — the wheel-crane detail specifically is plausible reconstruction, not directly attested.

bridge_restoration_2010_2018.claim: The bridge underwent a major restoration 2010–2018, documented by the Tiefbauamt Regensburg.

bridge_tower_history.claim: The bridge had 3 towers until 1784, 2 towers until ~1810, and 1 tower since then.
bridge_tower_history.notes: Internal production-planning figure only; no independent external primary source for the exact tower-count-by-year has been registered.

bruckmandl_location.claim: The Bruckmandl figure stands at the Scheitelpunkt (highest point) of the bridge, facing the Dom St. Peter.

bruckmandl_legend.claim: According to legend, the bridge's master builder made a wager with the cathedral's master builder and, as the cathedral progressed faster, is said to have made a pact with the devil.
bruckmandl_legend.notes: content_type: LEGEND — must always be presented as Sage/Legende, never as historical fact.

bruckmandl_interpretation.claim: The figure's exact historical meaning is not conclusively settled (interpretations range from a south/weather vane to a legendary depiction of the master builder).

bruckmandl_origin_year_1446.claim: The Bruckmandl figure's documented origin dates to 1446 (Jahr/Zeit der Entstehung).

bruckmandl_current_installed_1854.claim: The current (third) Bruckmandl figure was installed at its present location on 23 April 1854.

bruckmandl_sculptor_anton_blank.claim: The current figure was created by sculptor Anton Blank; the original (first) figure's sculptor is unknown.
bruckmandl_sculptor_anton_blank.notes: Both independently-verified official sources agree on 'Anton Blank'. An unregistered, unverified secondary claim (via Wikipedia, citing a 2018 academic chapter not yet consulted) names 'Andreas Blank (design) / Adam Poeverlein (execution)' instead — not registered here, not safe for public copy until reconciled against Q008 or another primary source.

bruckmandl_column_design_michael_mauerer.claim: The column/pedestal supporting the figure was designed by Michael Mauerer.

bruckmandl_material_original_gruensandst.claim: The original (first) Bruckmandl figure was made of Grünsandstein (green sandstone).

bruckmandl_material_current.claim: The material of the current (third) Bruckmandl figure.
bruckmandl_material_current.notes: CONFLICT: Q005 states the current figure's material as Kalkstein (limestone). Q006 calls the current figure a 'Sandsteinfigur' (sandstone) — a different rock type. Not resolved; do not state a specific material for the current figure in public copy until reconciled, ideally against Q008 (Bauer 1988, pp. 436-8, not yet directly consulted).

bruckmandl_destroyed_1579.claim: The original Bruckmandl figure was destroyed in 1579.

bruckmandl_third_figure_second_successor.claim: The current figure is the third figure of this name overall, i.e. the second successor of the original (destroyed 1579).

bruckmandl_second_figure_torso_museum.claim: The torso of the second Bruckmandl figure (the immediate predecessor of the current, third figure) survives in the Historisches Museum Regensburg.

bruckmandl_location_orientation_detail.claim: The figure sits on the western stone parapet at the bridge's highest point, approximately 11 metres above the river, facing south.
bruckmandl_location_orientation_detail.notes: Extends the existing bruckmandl_location claim (Q004, Q005) with the western-parapet and ~11m height detail.

bruckmandl_long_inscription_text.claim: The pedestal carries a long verse inscription, documented verbatim, referencing the bridge's 1135 construction start under Duke Heinrich and its completion after eleven years.
bruckmandl_long_inscription_text.notes: Exact wording quoted in Q006 (exhibition panel, pp. 5-6): 'Elf hundert drisig fünf im jahr / Die tonaw war schier trocken gar, / Der herzog heinrich mit der stat / Siw bruckn alhle begunen hat. / Das werck gebaut uft vesten grund / Eilf jar danach gantz fertig stund. / Gut gleit furbas uft allen wegen / Geb gots genad u. gotes Segen.' Safe to quote verbatim; do not add interpretation beyond what Q006 itself states.

bruckmandl_short_spruchband_text.claim: A short Spruchband beneath the figure's left hand carries the words "Schiuck wie hais …", documented as an abbreviation of a fuller saying preserved in an old manuscript of Kloster St. Emmeram, translated as "Ob kalt, ob heiß, zu Regensburg sind selbst die Häuter feist" (Häuter = emaciated horses).
bruckmandl_short_spruchband_text.notes: Existence and exact wording are SUPPORTED (quoted verbatim in Q006). Interpretation/meaning of the saying is tracked separately — see bruckmandl_short_spruchband_interpretation.

bruckmandl_short_spruchband_interpretati.claim: The meaning/interpretation of the short Spruchband saying.
bruckmandl_short_spruchband_interpretati.notes: content_type: INTERPRETATION. The exact wording is documented by the official Stadt Regensburg source, but its meaning remains unresolved.

bruckmandl_restoration_2012_2018.claim: The figure lost its right arm in 2012 (probable vandalism), was removed in 2014 for structural repair after foundation damage was found, stood as a placeholder until 2017, and was reinstalled restored on 5 June 2018.

bruckmandl_legend_chronologically_implau.claim: The city's own exhibition panel states that the builder's-wager/devil's-pact legend cannot literally be true, since the bridge (1135-1146) predates the cathedral's construction (begun in the second half of the 13th century) by roughly a century.
bruckmandl_legend_chronologically_implau.notes: This SUPPORTED status covers only the fact that the city's own source makes this chronological argument — it does not upgrade any part of the underlying legend itself, which remains content_type: LEGEND per the existing bruckmandl_legend claim above.

bruckmandl_shield_keys_identity.claim: The heraldic identity of the crossed-keys shield relief on the Bruckmandl pedestal.
bruckmandl_shield_keys_identity.notes: Not addressed by any registered source, including Q006, which was searched in full for 'Wappen'/'Schild'/'Schlüssel'/'Löwe'/'Relief' with zero matches. Do not infer this is Regensburg's city arms from visual resemblance alone, even though the city's own well-documented civic arms are two crossed silver keys on red — that is a separate, independently-documented general fact, not a statement about this specific pedestal.

bruckmandl_shield_lion_identity.claim: The heraldic identity of the lion shield relief on the Bruckmandl pedestal (rear face).
bruckmandl_shield_lion_identity.notes: Not addressed by any registered source. Do not conflate with the separate, differently-located sculpted lion elsewhere on the bridge (eastern balustrade above the 10th arch, marking historic Bavarian territorial authority) — that is a different object, not evidence about this pedestal's shield.

bruckmandl_interpretation_suedweiser.claim: One documented interpretation holds the figure to be a Südweiser (a figure shielding its eyes while looking south, functioning as a directional/weather indicator).
bruckmandl_interpretation_suedweiser.notes: content_type: INTERPRETATION — one of (at least) two open, officially-documented readings, per Q005 ('Seine Bedeutung ist bis heute nicht sicher geklärt'). Must never be presented as the settled or certain meaning of the figure.

bruckmandl_interpretation_civic_freedom.claim: The figure possibly symbolized, in medieval times, the Free Imperial City of Regensburg's freedom rights against the Bishop and the Duke of Bavaria.
bruckmandl_interpretation_civic_freedom.notes: content_type: INTERPRETATION — Q006 itself hedges this with 'Vermutlich' (presumably). Must never be presented as certain; keep the hedge in every language (e.g. 'vermutlich', 'presumably', 'posiblemente').

dom_gothic_background_rule.claim: The Gothic Dom St. Peter must not appear in the background before ~1275; before that, the Romanesque predecessor cathedral applies.
dom_gothic_background_rule.notes: Production/accuracy constraint, not itself a claim shown to visitors — governs which background asset may appear per K-frame date.

k06_dom_spire_visual_review.claim: K06 (dated 1140–1146) appears to show a visually complete Gothic cathedral spire in the background.
k06_dom_spire_visual_review.notes: Flagged VISUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED in KFRAMES_STORY_MAP.json (Phase 2.7C.4) as a possible inconsistency with dom_gothic_background_rule. Not resolved — image, date and source_ids intentionally left untouched pending a Visual Lab asset replacement.

k08_condition_unconfirmed.claim: K08's depicted repair/maintenance moment has no confirmed date or campaign.

k09_condition_unconfirmed.claim: K09's depicted moment has no confirmed date or historical placement.
